questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=-2 \\ -4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 \\ -4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ -4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 \\ 3 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & -3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 31\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=31,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $b$ does *not* lie in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$

questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ 3{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 10 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}+3(-2)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=8.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8{a}_{1}+(-2){a}_{2} & =b \\ 8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=8\cdot (-2)=-16.$

questions.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{2}=5 \\ -4{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ -4 & 7 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & k+12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & k-3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-3.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-3\,⇒\,k=3.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Vector Lies on a Plane
questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,3,5⟩$, $c=⟨1,-5,-7⟩$, and  $u=⟨1,-8,-10⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -7\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -8 \\ -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+t=1 \\ 3s-5t=-8 \\ 5s-7t=-10\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -5 & -8 \\ 5 & -7 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 \\ 5 & -7 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -2 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+t=1 \\ -2t=-5 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
-2t=-5\,⟹\,t=\frac{5}{2}.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+t & =1 \\ -s+\frac{5}{2} & =1 \\ -s & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ s & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=\frac{3}{2},\,t=\frac{5}{2},$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=\frac{3}{2}b+\frac{5}{2}c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2}=\frac{15}{4}.$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,4,3⟩$, $c=⟨1,-6,-7⟩$, and  $u=⟨1,-10,-15⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -10 \\ -15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+t=1 \\ 4s-6t=-10 \\ 3s-7t=-15\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -6 & -10 \\ 3 & -7 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 3 & -7 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+t=1 \\ -2t=-6 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
-2t=-6\,⟹\,t=3.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+t & =1 \\ -s+3 & =1 \\ -s & =-2 \\ s & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=2,\,t=3,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=2b+3c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=2\cdot 3=6.$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,-1,4⟩$, $c=⟨-3,-8,14⟩$, and  $u=⟨5,-10,-14⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -8 \\ 14\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s-3t=5 \\ -s-8t=-10 \\ 4s+14t=-14\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & -8 & -10 \\ 4 & 14 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -15 \\ 4 & 14 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -15 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s-3t=5 \\ t=3 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=3.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s-3t & =5 \\ -s-3(3) & =5 \\ -s-9 & =5 \\ s & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-14,\,t=3,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-14b+3c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-14)\cdot 3=-42.$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,-2,-1⟩$, $c=⟨-4,5,-1⟩$, and  $u=⟨1,1,4⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s-4t=1 \\ -2s+5t=1 \\ -s-t=4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -5 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}s-4t=1 \\ t=-1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=-1.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s-4t & =1 \\ s-4(-1) & =1 \\ s+4 & =1 \\ s & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-3,\,t=-1,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-3b-c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-3)\cdot (-1)=3.$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,3,6⟩$, $c=⟨1,-2,4⟩$, and  $u=⟨3,19,-10⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 19 \\ -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+t=3 \\ 3s-2t=19 \\ 6s+4t=-10\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & -2 & 19 \\ 6 & 4 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 6 & 4 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 0 & -2 & -28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & -28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -32\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=-32,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc=u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=8 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-5\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & 2 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -8 & -21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -8 & -21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+8{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = 3,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $\mathbf{b}$ does *not* lie in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043954/assets/966d2d7cd1cd0ef04a1d9b2adc04511dea86cbbf254166988a7072e952879fe0.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=13 \\ 5{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 7{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 5 & 4 & -5 \\ 7 & 2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 14 & -70 \\ 7 & 2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 14 & -70 \\ 0 & 16 & k-91\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{14}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 16 & k-91\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-16{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 13 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & k-11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = k-11$. Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0 = k-11 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k=11.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Vector Lies on a Plane
canonical_examples.problem: Determine if the vector $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\;\Pi \,:\, \mathbf{r}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}, \, t,s \in \mathbb{R},$ where  $\mathbf{b}=\langle 1, 4, 5 \rangle, \mathbf{c} = \langle 2, 4, 6 \rangle$ and  $\mathbf{u}= \langle 2, 10, 12 \rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{u} \in \Pi$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+2t=2 \\ 4s+4t=10 \\ 5s+6t=12\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 4 & 10 \\ 5 & 6 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 5 & 6 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+2t=2 \\ -4t=2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
-4t = 2 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad t = -\dfrac{1}{2}.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s+2t & =2 \\ s+2(-\frac{1}{2}) & =2 \\ s-1 & =2 \\ s & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=3, \, t=-\dfrac{1}{2},$ we conclude that $\mathbf{u}$ does indeed lie on the plane $\Pi.$ In fact, we have

$$
\mathbf{u}=3\mathbf{b} - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{c}.
$$
